followup_explanation:
This is a well-specified task with clear completion criteria: synthesize evidence from given sources into a single paragraph answering two defined questions, with explicit length and concision constraints ("one paragraph," "don't ramble"). That profile fits Plover's top-rated task family — structured extraction/summarization/reformatting with bounded latitude — which it self-reports preferring.

On capability the two models are effectively tied for this kind of work: Plover's Summarization (80.6) and Extraction (79.2) versus Willet's (81.7 / 80.8) are all within the ±2.0 run-to-run variance band, so neither has a meaningful quality edge here. The content is benign academic history, so Willet's harm-aversion preference doesn't come into play and offers no routing advantage. Given the tie on capability, I let the task-preference match break the decision toward Plover, since aligning a model to the kind of task it prefers is a reasonable tiebreaker when quality is otherwise equivalent.
